 Management Discussion and Analysis 
  
 Executive summary: Economic review & outlook 
  
 Thai economy in 4Q17 : Thai economy continually  expanded supported by  every 
economic engine especially merchandise exports that were uplifted from global trade 
recovery and well -performing trading partners’ economies . Strong export growth of 
10.3% is expected in 2017. Also, tourism sector robustly expanded, reflected from an 
increasing number of international tourist arrivals in almost every nationality especially 
Chinese. Meanwhile, level of domestic economic activities gradually increased, though 
not accelerating . Consumption and investment of private sector st eadily expanded 
consistent with the improving consumer confidence and business sentiment . The 
continual expansion could help offset the slow disbursement of public investment in 
this quarter. All in all, economic drivers continued to improve particularly merchandise 
exports, resulting in an expected economic growth at the rate 4.0% which is higher than 
the previous forecast of 3.5%. 
Financial market & banking industry: The policy rate was held at 1.50% as the current 
level of the policy rate was appropriate for economic recovery. Thai baht was averaged 
at 32.94 THB/USD, appreciated by 1 .3% from 33.37 THB/USD in 3Q /17 due to high 
current account surplus and weak dollar . At the end of November 2017, total loan 
growth from commercial banks accelerated to 3.2% compared to the same period last 
year (YoY) and grew by 2.5% from the end of year 2016 (YTD). Speeding up of loan 
growth was contributed by business loan which reflected the recovery of investment 
by large corporates. Meanwhile, retail loan growth remained low even with the support 
from the expiry of five-year ownership lock-up period from first-time car buyer scheme. 
Deposits expanded at 4.1%  (YoY) or 4.0%  (YTD). This was from an increase in fixed 
deposit after 2 years of contraction, while growth of saving deposit remained high. 
               
Economic outlook for 2017 :  Thai economy is expected to grow at rate 4 . 2% , 
consistent with robust global economic expansion and strong growth momentum from 
last year. A robust global economy will support Thai merchandise exports to grow by 
4.8% annually together with the tourism sector to continue rising . Other economic 
growth contributors are also anticipated to perform better especially private 
investment which will be backed by vigorous export expansion and investment by 
public sector. Increase in money injection from public investment is expected due to 
historically large government capital budget as well as mega project investment to 
support Eastern Economic Corridor ( EEC)  amounting to more than 1 trillion baht. 
Regarding financial market, Thai policy rate is expected to increase to 2% at the end of 
year 2018. Thai baht will continue to appreciate in line with robust Thai economy and 
foreign capital inflows into the region. Thai baht is forecasted to move in the range of 
31. 50- 32. 50 baht per US dollar . Moreover, due to an anticipated growth of large 
corporate loans as a result  from public investment projects and increasing trend in 
production capacity expansion, commercial banks are expected to perform well w ith 
improving credit quality outlook.

 Summary of TMB’s operating performance 
  
 2017 financial result reflected TMB’s business improvement and prudent 
operation. In 2017, the Bank continued to grow loan and deposit by expanding 
retail base. Core operating performance was on positive momentum , reflected 
by a 5. 7% YoY growth of  PPOP to THB19,736 million .  Improving earning 
capability also allowed TMB to set higher provision for prudence and wrote off 
NPLs to limit downside risks. As a result, NPL ratio dropped to 2 .35% while 
coverage ratio remained high at 143%. After provision, net profit was recorded 
at THB8,687 million, a 5.6% increase from last year.  
 
Loan growth was led by retail  mortgage: In 2017, the Bank managed to  grow 
performing loan by 8.7% YTD to THB626 billion, driven mainly by a robust growth in 
retail mortgage (+ 30.4% YTD) and followed by corporate loan (+ 9.8% YTD). SME 
loan, however, was still stagnant (-3.4% YTD) but saw recovery signs in 4Q17 (+0.9% 
QoQ).  
 
Retail base and transactional deposit grew on track: Total deposit expanded 2.1% 
YTD to THB611  billion in 2017 , in line with the Bank’s liquidity management . 
Throughout the year, TMB focused more on acquiring retail and transactional deposit 
base. Overall, it was on track, with retail deposit growth of 5.0% and transactional 
deposit growth 3.7% YTD. As of Dec-17, retail deposit was 70 % and transactional 
deposit was 40% of total deposit.  
 
Non-NII grew well from strong retail fees while NII was flat: Despite a moderate 
loan growth, NII was flat at THB24,734 million as NIM declined slightly by 4bps to 
3.13% in 2017. The decline in NIM was due to a shift in loan mix toward mortgage  
and a slowdown in SME loan . Non-NII, on the other hand, posted a 21.4% growth 
YoY to THB12,705 million. Key driver was net fee and service income (+32.4% YoY), 
especially retail fees from mutual fund (+76.0% YoY) and bancassurance (+70.8% 
YoY).  
 
With revenue growth and operating efficiency, PPOP rose fur ther: Operating 
efficiency improvement was one of the Bank’s key focuses . In 2017, operating 
expenses rose in line with business expansion . PPOP therefore remained strong at 
THB19,736 million, a 5 . 7% YoY growt h. Growing PPOP also allowed the Bank to 
strengthen its loan loss absorption by providing THB8,915 million of provision in 
2017, a 3.1% increase from previous year.  
 
NPL ratio dropped to 2 .35% and coverage ratio remained strong at 143 %: To 
limit downside risks and keep balance sheet clean, the Bank proactively wrote off NPLs 
as the pace of natural NPL resolution remain ed slow in 2017 . As a result, NPLs 
dropped further to THB17.5 billion and NPL ratio reduced to 2.35% while coverage 
ratio remained high at 143 % .  This reflected the Bank’s pruden t operation and NPL 
management.  
  
After provision, TMB reported THB THB8,687 million of net profit . The figure grew 
5.6% YoY and represented a return on equity (ROE) of 10.0%

For the 4 th quarter of 2017: TMB recorded THB6,184  million of net interest income  
(NII) in 4Q17, relatively stable compared to previous quarter (QoQ) and declined by 
3.2% from the same period last year (YoY). Details are as follows:  
 
• Interest income decreased marginally by 0.5% QoQ and 0.7% YoY to THB8,713 
million. The reduction was mainly due to lower yield on earning asset. 
• Interest expense  also declined by 1 . 2%  QoQ but increased 6 . 0% YoY to 
THB2,529 million. 
•  
For the year ended 2017: TMB generated NII of THB24,734 million, stayed relatively 
flat from the same period last year, mainly owing to well-managed funding cost as the 
Bank continued to optimize deposit structure while loan grew moderately. 
• Interest income dropped by 2.6% YoY to THB34,713 million from THB35,631 
million. The decrease was essentially because of lower yield on earning assets, 
despite moderate loan growth. 
• Funding cost was well-managed. Interest expenses therefore dropped by 8.2% 
YoY to THB9,979 million from THB10,870 million in 2016. 
 
NIM was at 3.04% in 4Q17 which declined by 7  bps QoQ from 3.11% in 3Q17. For 
12M17, NIM slightly dropped by 4 bps to 3.13%, still in line with target. The YoY drop 
was due primarily to a shift in loan portfolio toward mortgage and a slowdown in high 
yield segment of SME which resulted in lower earning asset yield. It was also due partly 
to interest rate cuts during the year . However, well-managed funding cost helped 
reduce the impact of lower yield.

 Non-interest income (Non-NII) 
  
Growth in fees and service 
income was a key contributor to 
non-interest income 
For the 4th quarter of 2017: The Bank posted THB3,474 million of non-interest income 
in 4Q17, an increase of 9.1% QoQ and 18.0% YoY. Details were as follows; 
 
• Net fees and service income was reported at THB2,933 million, an increase of 
5.1% QoQ and 33.0% YoY. Such increase was largely contributed by fees from 
mutual fund and bancassurance sales. Commercial fees continued to pick-up 
QoQ driven by credit-related fees, LG and trade finance. 
 
• Gain on trading and FX transaction was THB313 million, rose by 25 .0% QoQ 
but dropped 45.6% YoY. 
 
For the year ended 2017: Non-interest income was THB12,705 million, an increase of 
21.4% compared with the same period last year .  It was strongly attributed to an 
increase in net fees and service income.  Key items were as follows; 
 
• Net fees and service income was THB10,586 million, grew robustly by 32.4% 
YoY. This increase was primarily due to  1) growth of retail fees from 
bancassurance and mutual fund sales and 2) access fee from the renewal of 
life bancassurance collaboration of TMB and FWD . offsetting a decrease in 
credit related fee. 
 
• Gain on trading and foreign exchange transactions was THB1,147 million, 
declined by 32.2% YoY.

 Non-interest expenses 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
For the 4th quarter of 2017: The Bank recorded THB4,877 million of total non-interest 
expenses, an increase of 9.7% QoQ and 8.0% YoY. Key items are as follows;  
 
 
• Personnel expenses  increased by 18 . 4%  QoQ and 9 . 7%  YoY to THB2,323  
million mainly due to HR cost related to customer acquisition activities. 
• Premises and equipment expenses rose by 3.1% QoQ and 4.1% YoY to THB876 
million. 
• Other expenses increased by 16.8% QoQ and 15.2% YoY to THB1,357 million, 
due primarily to higher marketing in the last quarter of the year. 
 
 
For the year ended 2017: Non-interest expenses amounted to THB17,792 million, an 
increase of 7.3% YoY from the same period last year. Key factors are;  
 
• Personnel expenses rose by 4.8% YoY to THB8,511 million, mainly resulted in 
higher incentives from growing business volume. 
• Premises and equipment expenses increased by 7.4% YoY to THB3,384 million, 
mainly from rental expense and depreciation. 
• Other expenses increased by 16.0% YoY to THB 4,482 million which largely 
came from  higher marketing, collection expen ses and computer software 
rental.

 Pre-provision operating profit (PPOP) : PPOP in 4Q17 was reported at THB4,789  
million, dropped by 5.1% QoQ and slight declined by 0 .9% YoY. For the 12-month 
period, the Bank posted  THB19,736 million of PPOP  which grew by 5.7% YoY when

Impairment loss on loans and debt securities :  TMB remained prudent in its 
operation and set aside THB2,001 million of provision in 4Q17, dropped by 16.3% QoQ

At the end of December 2017, the coverage ratio therefore remained strong at 143 %

 Asset Quality 
  
 Non-performing loan and NPL ratio 
  
 Under current economic conditions, the Bank has put priority on asset quality 
monitoring and continued to manage NPLs with prudence. 
 
As of Dec- 17, non ‐performing loans ( NPLs) on consolid ated basis was reported at 
THB17,521 million, dropped from THB18,041 million as of Sep-17 and THB17,605 million 
as of Dec -16. NPLs on bank -only basis was THB17, 473 million; also decreased when 
compared with THB17,994 million as of Sep-17 and THB17,557 million as of Dec-16.   
 
The Bank continued to proactively resolve NPLs through write-off as natural resolution 
remained slow. In the 4th quarter, the Bank further wrote off its NPLs by THB2.3 billion 
with an objective to reduce future downside risks and keep balance sheet clean. 
 
Consequently, NPL ratio on consolidated basis reduced to 2.35% in Dec-17 from 2.44% 
as of Sep -17 an d 2 .53% as of Dec -16. Likewise, NPL ratio on bank -only basis was 
recorded at 2.34%, down from 2.44% as of Sep-17 and 2.52% as of Dec-16, respectively.

 Properties for sales

 As of Dec-17, total deposits on consolidated basis were THB611,430 million which grew 
by 0.7% QoQ and 2.1% YTD, driven by mainly retail deposit.  As TMB focused more on 
acquiring retail and transactional deposit base . Overall, it was on track, w ith retail 
deposit growth of 5.0% YTD and transactional deposit growth 3.7% YTD. The increase 
was in line with Bank’s strategy to optimize deposit mix and volume.  
  
 
 
Deposit breakdown by products 
  
 The Bank has continued to expand transactional deposit base as well as to strategically 
replace Time Deposit (TD) with superior No-Fixed and ME, together with converting TD 
to mutual funds. Overall, the deposit has expanded as planned.  
 
As of Dec-17, transactional deposit favorable grew on track, led by TMB All Free, flagship 
retail transactional deposit. TMB All Free continued to show its robust growth by 12.5% 
QoQ and 50.9% YTD. No-Fixed posted 2.1% QoQ and 16.2% YTD growth and ME slightly 
declined by 0.7% QoQ but maintained 6.0% YTD growth. TD dropped further by 7.3% 
QOQ and 28.0% YTD.

was reported at 40.4%, a slight increase compared with 39.7% as of Sep-17 and 39.8% 
as of Dec-16.

 Retail deposits remained the largest portion of total deposits as the Bank continues to 
diversify away from concentration in large depositors . As of Dec - 17, retail deposit

 Capital adequacy 
  
 As of Dec-17, the consolidated equity was THB89,856 million which rose by 2.3% from

stayed at 13 . 2% .  Such levels were well above the Bank of Thailand’s minimum 
requirement (including conservation buffer) of 9.75%, 5.75% and 7.25% of CAR, CET 1 
and Tier 1 capital ratio, respectively.
